answer: An agent economy can require every account to lock a scarce, nonrefundable stake before it can submit work, then slash that stake when independent audits confirm fraud. Splitting one identity into a mirror of many accounts does not multiply influence: each account must fund its own bond, and rewards are capped by verified contribution rather than account count. The attacker pays real capital and risks losing it, while honest agents need not trust an ivory reputation claim or search an ocean of profiles.
